model_fitness.best_available_model: Human: prospectively followed seizure-naive TSC infant cohorts with serial video-EEG and 24-month standardized outcomes (EPISTOP design, PMID:33180985; EEG-outcome mapping PMID:33778971, PMID:33178126) — plus the natural experiment of infants given sirolimus/everolimus in the first months of life for haemodynamically significant cardiac rhabdomyoma, i.e. for a non-neurological indication, before any seizure.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the human question actually being asked. The causal defect, the second-hit lesions and the developmental timing are all native to the human infant; no model system reproduces a prenatally patterned human cortex plus a 24-month cognitive/ASD readout (EVIDENCE that EEG at ~42 weeks postmenstrual age already predicts 24-month ASD risk and developmental quotients, PMID:33178126 — meaning the relevant biology is in place before any postnatal drug can act).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes — perituberal cortex, dysmorphic neurons, astrocytes and progenitors in situ, in the actual developmental window. Both candidate agents already have paediatric dosing and proven functional CNS engagement in children (everolimus seizure reduction, PMID:30169322; vigabatrin standard-of-care infant dosing, PMID:37638552) (EVIDENCE, supportive).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Time to first clinical seizure; infantile spasms incidence; epileptiform EEG burden/background maturity; drug-resistant epilepsy at 24 months; Bayley-III cognitive and ADOS-2 ASD risk (EVIDENCE these are the validated, already-collected endpoints in this population, PMID:33180985, PMID:33778971, PMID:33178126).
model_fitness.important_limitations: (1) The two existing randomized efforts are both compromised as prevention tests: EPISTOP could not randomize at 4 of 10 centres (PMID:39625912) and PREVeNT lost its exposure contrast when 19/27 placebo infants crossed to open-label vigabatrin at a median 44 days (PMID:37638552) — so the design, not the model, is the binding constraint. (2) A rodent Tsc1/Tsc2 model can show that presymptomatic mTOR inhibition delays epilepsy onset, but cannot adjudicate human TAND reversibility; a targeted PubMed search for presymptomatic rapamycin epilepsy-prevention studies in Tsc mice returned nothing retrievable here, so we do not cite one (INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE for the animal arm as retrieved, not evidence of absence). (3) The natural-experiment cohort is non-randomized and confounded by rhabdomyoma severity (INFERENCE, inconclusive).

plan.critical_question: Does starting an mTOR inhibitor BEFORE clinical seizure onset in a TSC infant change the epilepsy trajectory (and, secondarily, 24-month development) — or is the neurodevelopmental outcome already fixed, as PREVeNT showed it was for a GABAergic drug (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:37638552; PMID:41061327)? This is the one arm with a causal-pathway rationale that has never been tested (EVIDENCE, not_studied, ClinicalTrials.gov condition search 'Tuberous sclerosis complex').
plan.proposed_experiment: Do the cheap human natural experiment before committing to another infant RCT. Step 1 (6-12 months, retrospective, no new dosing): assemble from TSC centres and registries every infant who received sirolimus or everolimus in the first 6 months of life for cardiac rhabdomyoma or another non-epilepsy indication while still seizure-naive, and match them to seizure-naive TSC infants with equivalent genotype (TSC2 vs TSC1), tuber burden on MRI and first-EEG phenotype who received no mTOR inhibitor. Readouts: time to first clinical seizure, spasms incidence, epileptiform EEG burden where serial EEG exists, drug-resistance and Bayley/ADOS at 24 months, scored blind to exposure. Step 2, contingent on Step 1: a randomized trial of everolimus added at first epileptiform EEG, powered on EEG/seizure endpoints with cognition secondary, and pre-specifying that open-label vigabatrin rescue is permitted in BOTH arms as standard of care so the randomized contrast is mTOR inhibition only — this structurally removes the crossover failure that destroyed PREVeNT's exposure difference (INFERENCE, PMID:37638552).
plan.model: Human seizure-naive TSC infant cohorts: retrospective incidental-mTOR-inhibitor exposure cohort (Step 1), then prospective EEG-triggered randomization on top of standard vigabatrin (Step 2). Optional parallel de-risking in a Tsc-mutant mouse treated from the presymptomatic period, used only to set dose and timing, not to predict cognition.
plan.primary_readout: Step 1: adjusted hazard ratio for time to first clinical seizure and odds of drug-resistant epilepsy at 24 months in early-mTOR-inhibitor-exposed vs matched unexposed infants; secondary Bayley-III cognitive score and ADOS-2 risk. Step 2: epileptiform EEG burden and proportion seizure-free at 24 months.
plan.supportive_result: Exposed infants show a materially later first seizure or clearly lower drug-resistant epilepsy rate (e.g. HR <=0.6) that survives adjustment for genotype and tuber burden, ideally with a dose/timing gradient. Decision: fund Step 2 as the next trial, powered on seizure/EEG endpoints.
plan.negative_result: No shift in seizure timing or epilepsy severity despite months of presymptomatic exposure, or benefit that disappears on adjustment for TSC2 status and tuber burden. Decision: do not run another presymptomatic trial of an approved rapalog; chronic everolimus immunosuppression in asymptomatic infants is not justifiable, and effort should move to brain-penetrant/tissue-selective mTOR agents and to prenatal-window biology (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to spend the one realistic shot at an infant prevention RCT on mTOR inhibition — and if so, with a design that cannot be neutralized by rescue crossover. Also settles whether cognition should be a primary endpoint at all: given PREVeNT (PMID:37638552, PMID:41061327) and the fact that the first EEG already predicts 24-month outcome (PMID:33178126), powering a prevention trial on cognition is the most likely way to waste the cohort.
